# Garamba’s Population of Kordofan Giraffe is Growing – Here’s Why

Conserving Kordofan giraffe requires a partnership-based approach to conserve landscapes like Garamba National Park in DRC, plus innovations in wildlife monitoring and genetic research.



 © Marcus Westberg 

 6 minute read 

_Innovations in giraffe conservation methodologies are having a positive impact on the Kordofan giraffe population in DRC’s Garamba National Park._

Garamba National Park is home to the only population of giraffe in DRC, and no ordinary giraffe at that. The Kordofan giraffe (named for the Kordofan region of central Sudan) is a subspecies of the northern giraffe, one of four recognised giraffe species.

The latest phylogenetic studies have shown that there are in fact a total of seven extant subspecies of giraffe. While many of them are superficially similar, they can be told apart by differences in their skin markings, and their relative sizes (the Kordofan giraffe is slightly smaller, on average, than other giraffe subspecies).

Most importantly, each of the subspecies occupies distinct geographical areas in Africa. In the case of the Kordofan giraffe, this is the savannah regions of the Sahel and Central Africa. Geographical distribution is a clue to the importance of classifying different species of giraffe; without this level of understanding, the real significance of declines in individual populations or local extinctions might not be fully appreciated.

(Interestingly, the Kordofan giraffe was previously known as the Congo giraffe – _Giraffa camelopardalis congolensis_ – but has since been reclassified as _Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum_. ‘Congo giraffe’ is a term that is also sometimes used to describe the okapi, a species that is related to giraffe).

## Garamba – a stronghold for the Kordofan giraffe

![Image 1](https://www.africanparks.org/sites/default/files/styles/inline_image_style/public/teaser_image/2026-06/250327_By%20Rodolphe%20Lutengya.jpg?itok=7m-HLjYu)© Radolphe Lutengya

There are only around 7,000 northern giraffe left in the wild, making it one of the most threatened large mammals on Earth. Of these, approximately 2,400 belong to the Kordofan subspecies, which is listed by the IUCN as Critically Endangered. With around 50% of these in just one national park – Zakouma in Chad – there’s a clear need to establish viable populations in other protected landscapes, including Garamba.

Only in this way can the resilience of the subspecies be enhanced and maintained, especially given the threats that all giraffe species face. Habitat loss and illegal hunting are the main risks, although in the case of Garamba, local cultural taboos against hunting and eating giraffe help to keep the Kordofan population safe.

## The fall and rise of giraffe in Garamba

Despite this, giraffe have previously come close to local extinction in Garamba. From an estimated population of 350 giraffe in the 1970s, only 22 remained in 2012, with illegal hunting again being the main factor behind this decline in numbers.

Historically, giraffe occurred throughout the Garamba Complex. Today, the population persists in two geographically distinct breeding groups: one in the southern sector of Garamba National Park and another in Gangala na Bodio Hunting Domain. Overall numbers of Kordofan giraffe in Garamba have risen to an estimated 105 at the last count (in April 2025; more on counting giraffe later in this blog).

## Partnering in Conserving the Kordofan Giraffe

Conservation of giraffe – or any species – is best achieved through long-term partnerships. In the case of Garamba and its giraffe population, stakeholders including the ICCN, specialist NGO Giraffe Conservation Foundation (GCF), DRC wildlife authorities and African Parks have been collaborating since 2012.

The partnership between Garamba National Park and the Giraffe Conservation Foundation was formalised in 2022 and renewed in 2025 through a second, three-year agreement designed to provide ongoing financial and technical support.

## Science-based, data-driven conservation in partnership with GCF

![Image 2](https://www.africanparks.org/sites/default/files/styles/inline_image_style/public/teaser_image/2026-06/250316_By%20Davy%20Fonteyn.jpg?itok=4RzV7d8H)© Davy Fonteyn

The technical aspects of giraffe conservation in Garamba include innovations in aerial monitoring, based on the implementation of a new giraffe monitoring strategy devised by Giraffe Conservation Foundation. Beginning in 2025, Garamba introduced a dedicated aerial monitoring protocol designed specifically for giraffe – one of the first of its kind in the world.The monitoring programme has a target of observing at least 80% of Garamba’s population of Kordofan giraffe every six months.

Ultralight Savannah aircraft have transformed the work of aerial surveys by providing a more cost-effective platform from which to monitor the animals. Surveys are flown along planned transects in the areas where the giraffe tend to spend their time.

The results have been encouraging, with this approach having achieved an 89% detection rate, with a median of four sightings per individual during the year. AI-driven GiraffeSpotter – Wildbook for Giraffe software and databases, supplied by the GCF, also enables the identification of individual giraffe, and greatly enhances the value that can be extracted from monitoring and survey data.

## It’s in their genes

![Image 3](https://www.africanparks.org/sites/default/files/styles/inline_image_style/public/teaser_image/2026-06/20250717_GIR05FA%20_By%20Jackson%20Mumbere%20Kasogho.jpg?itok=JHE7_orI)© Jackson Munbere Kasogho

Genetic and morphology studies have played an important part in the story of modern giraffe conservation. Geneticists helped to solve the riddle of how many giraffe species and subspecies there are, and, at park level, are enabling a better understanding of the genetic health and long-term viability of populations such as Garamba’s Kordofan giraffe.

Currently, 27 giraffe skin biopsy samples are undergoing laboratory analysis, facilitated and supported by Giraffe Conservation Foundation. This process will provide important information on genetic diversity, inbreeding risk, and the long-term viability of the two isolated breeding populations. The results will help inform future management decisions and conservation planning in Garamba and beyond.

## Garamba’s giraffe today

From a population reduced to just 22 individuals in 2012, following decades of civil unrest, illegal hunting, and habitat degradation,Garamba’s giraffe population continues to recover. Sustained partnership-based conservation efforts have contributed to this steady recovery, with 70 individuals confirmed in 2021, 92 in 2024, and an estimated 105 in 2025.It is hoped that such collaborative conservation efforts will see this positive trend continue and even accelerate.

## Why the Kordofan giraffe matters

![Image 4](https://www.africanparks.org/sites/default/files/styles/inline_image_style/public/teaser_image/2026-06/20250928_By%20Davy%20Fonteyn%20%282%29.jpg?itok=UL-Pp8zf)© Davy Fonteyn 

It’s not only about the giraffe. At a macro level, Kordofan giraffe have, like other giraffe, an added significance as biodiversity indicators, with their presence or absence showing the relative health of a habitat or wider ecosystem.

In addition, like other giraffe species, the Kordofan giraffe is an ‘ecosystem engineer’ – that is, it helps to shape the habitat around it, and boosts biodiversity. Giraffe browsing habits prevent vegetation overgrowth, promote diversity of plant and tree species, and allow more sunlight to reach lower-growing vegetation.

Effective conservation measures for the Kordofan giraffe depend on massive, interconnected protected landscapes and conservation at an ecosystem rather than a species level. This in turn will help to conserve other species that depend on the same habitat.

Garamba National Park in northeast DRC is home to critically endangered Kordofan giraffes, forest elephants, hippos, and lions — one of Africa's oldest and most exclusive national parks, managed by African Parks with zero tourist crowds.

Quick Answer

**Yes, there are giraffes in the DRC.** Garamba National Park hosts Kordofan giraffes (Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum) — one of the rarest giraffe subspecies. The park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site established in 1938, covering 4,902 km² in northeast DRC's Haut-Uélé Province.

The **Kordofan giraffe** (_Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum_) is one of the most endangered giraffe subspecies in the world, with fewer than 2,000 individuals remaining in the wild. Garamba National Park in northeast DRC is one of its last strongholds.

African Parks, in partnership with ICCN (Congo's wildlife authority), has significantly improved the park's security and infrastructure since 2005, creating conditions for wildlife recovery and limited but growing tourism access.

Charter flights to Nagero airstrip (inside the park) from Entebbe (Uganda) or Kisangani. Overland access from Dungu for adventurous travelers. Most visitors fly via Entebbe.

### Best Time to Visit

November–March (dry season) for optimal wildlife viewing. May–September is greener but some roads may be impassable. Avoid April and October (peak rains).

### Where to Stay

Nagero Rest House (managed by African Parks) is the primary accommodation. Tented camping options available. Remote lodge development is part of ongoing investment plans.

### Permits & Access

Entry permits issued by African Parks / ICCN. All visits require advance booking. Armed ranger escort included in all safari activities for visitor safety.

November–March (dry season) for optimal wildlife viewing. May–September is greener but some roads may be impassable. Avoid April and October (peak rains).

Nagero Rest House (managed by African Parks) is the primary accommodation. Tented camping options available. Remote lodge development is part of ongoing investment plans.

Entry permits issued by African Parks / ICCN. All visits require advance booking. Armed ranger escort included in all safari activities for visitor safety.

The **Kordofan giraffe** (_**Giraffa antiquorum**_[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:1-2) or _**Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum**_) is a [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species "Species") or [subspecies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subspecies "Subspecies") of [giraffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giraffe "Giraffe") found in [northern Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Cameroon "Northern Cameroon"), southern [Chad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad "Chad"), the [Central African Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_African_Republic "Central African Republic"), and possibly [western Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Sudan "Western Sudan").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-range-3) They usually live in [tree savannas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna"), [bush savannas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steppe "Steppe") and [thorn savannas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4) Compared to most other subspecies, the Kordofan giraffe is relatively small at 3.8 to 4.7 m (12 ft 6 in to 15 ft 5 in),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-5) with more irregular spots on the inner legs. There are around 2,300 individuals living in the wild.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-6) In the wild, female Kordofan giraffes live in loose groups, whilst males live solitary.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4) They have an average lifespan of around 35 years.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)

_[The Christian Science Monitor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Christian\_Science\_Monitor "The Christian Science Monitor")_ lists only 38 individuals being alive in the embattled [Garamba National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park "Garamba National Park") in [The Democratic Republic of Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Democratic_Republic_of_Congo "The Democratic Republic of Congo") due to [poaching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poaching "Poaching"); their skin is used for [luxury goods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxury_goods "Luxury goods") and they are said to produce enough meat to feed poachers for weeks.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Recent genetic studies also shows distinct [genetic populations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_populations "Genetic populations") of giraffes that makes conservation of these subspecies even more important.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-7)

The population in the Bénoué Complex, Cameroon (a landscape that consists of three national parks: [Bénoué National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9nou%C3%A9_National_Park "Bénoué National Park"), [Faro National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faro_National_Park "Faro National Park"), [Bouba Njida National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bouba_Njida_National_Park "Bouba Njida National Park"); interconnected by 29 hunting zones), numbers fewer than 300 individuals as of 2023.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-onlinelibrary.wiley.com-8) Illegal hunting represents the greatest threat to the subspecies, particularly in [Bénoué National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9nou%C3%A9_National_Park "Bénoué National Park"), where it may become locally extinct without further conservation interventions.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-onlinelibrary.wiley.com-8)

The Kordofan giraffe eats a variety of sticks, leaves and bark, usually of [Acacia trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acacia "Acacia"). Additionally they eat grasses, buds, as well as seeds.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Like other giraffes, they classify as herbivores.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)

## Taxonomy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Taxonomy")]

Its English name is a reference to [Kordofan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan "Kordofan") in [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan "Sudan").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:1-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-range-3)

## Habitat

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Habitat")]

They are naturally found in northern [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon "Cameroon"), [Chad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad "Chad"), [Central African Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_African_Republic "Central African Republic") and [western Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan_(region) "Sudan (region)").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-range-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Kordofan giraffe live in [steppes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steppe "Steppe"), as well as [bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna"), [tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna") and [shrub savannas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4) Historically some confusion has existed over the exact range limit of this subspecies compared to the [West African giraffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_African_giraffe "West African giraffe"), with populations in e.g. northern [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon "Cameroon") formerly assigned to the latter.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Genetic work has also revealed that all "[West African giraffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_African_giraffe "West African giraffe")" in European [zoos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoo "Zoo") are in fact Kordofan giraffe.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) It has been suggested that the [Nigerian giraffe's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_African_giraffe "West African giraffe") ancestor dispersed from East to North Africa during the [Quaternary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaternary "Quaternary") period and thereafter migrated to its current [Sahel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahel "Sahel") distribution in West Africa in response to the development of the [Sahara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahara "Sahara") desert.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-range-3)

## Appearance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Appearance")]

The Kordofan giraffe has spots similarly to other giraffe subspecies. They are [even-toed ungulates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artiodactyl "Artiodactyl") and walk on long legs. Compared to other subspecies they are rather small; males are on average 6 m (19 ft 8 in) tall, females reach a height of 4.5 m (14 ft 9 in).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Their shoulder height lies between 2 metres (6 ft 7 in) for females to 3.5 metres (11 ft 6 in) for males.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) On top of that they have more irregular spots on the inner legs.

They have a blue tongue, which is around 50 centimetres (1 ft 8 in) long.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)

## Diet

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Diet")]

Like other giraffe subspecies, the Kordofan giraffe is a [herbivore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbivore "Herbivore"). Its diet consist of a variety of grasses, shrubs, buds, branches, leaves and bark, as well as seeds.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Their main food source comes from the [Acacia trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acacia "Acacia").

## Conservation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Conservation")]

Kordofan giraffe is one of most endangered giraffe subspecies. The population of kordofan giraffe declined more than 80% for last 35 years, IUCN Red List has classified the Kordofan giraffe as Critically Endangered species in 2018.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFchad-10)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-iucn-1)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Kordofan_giraffe_in_Garamba_National_Park.jpg/250px-Kordofan_giraffe_in_Garamba_National_Park.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kordofan_giraffe_in_Garamba_National_Park.jpg)

Kordofan giraffe in the [Garamba National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park "Garamba National Park"), DRC

In the [Garamba National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park "Garamba National Park") in DRC, their population was declined from 300 in 1976 to 100 in 2008.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-11) Another estimate is from 356 in 1993 to only 86 in 2007.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-thetimes-12) There also estimate that 86 in 2003 and only 38 in 2016.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-13) Most recent estimate is from 71 in 2022 to over 80 in 2024.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-14) Poaching is the greatest threat to Garamba's giraffe population.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-thetimes-12)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCF_DRC-15) It has brought Giraffe Conservation Foundation (GCF) collaboration with ICCN and African Parks and DRC's wildlife authority to save last giraffes in DRC since 2016.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCF_DRC-15) Fortunately, DRC government have successfully increased in Kordofan giraffe population in park to more than 90 individuals.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCF_DRC-15)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7d/Waza-NP-Giraffes.jpg/250px-Waza-NP-Giraffes.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Waza-NP-Giraffes.jpg)

A group of Kordofan giraffes in the [Waza National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waza_National_Park "Waza National Park"), Cameroon

In Bénoué Complex on Cameroon(a landscape that consists of three national parks: [Bénoué National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9nou%C3%A9_National_Park "Bénoué National Park"), [Faro National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faro_National_Park "Faro National Park"), [Bouba Njida National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bouba_Njida_National_Park "Bouba Njida National Park")); interconnected by 29 hunting zones), it is estimated fewer than 300 population remained in 2023. Illegal hunting is a major threat to giraffe in the Bénoué National Park, where it may become locally extinct without further conservation efforts.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-16) In an aerial survey by Wildlife Conservation Society of [Waza National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waza_National_Park "Waza National Park") it was revealed that at least 350 individuals remained.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFcameroon-17) GCF drafting the first-ever National Giraffe Conservation Strategy and Action Plan with together Cameroon government, to help conservation efforts for Kordofan giraffe in the country.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFcameroon-17)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ee/Girafe_du_parc_national_de_Zakouma.jpg/250px-Girafe_du_parc_national_de_Zakouma.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Girafe_du_parc_national_de_Zakouma.jpg)

Kordofan giraffe in the [Zakouma National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zakouma_National_Park "Zakouma National Park"), Chad

[Zakouma National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zakouma_National_Park "Zakouma National Park") of [Chad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad "Chad") is home to 60% of Kordofan giraffe remaining on earth.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFchad-10) According to a series of aerial surveys in park between 2005 and 2016, population of giraffe in park increased from 292 to 947.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-iucn-1) GCF drafting the first-ever conservation efforts for Kordofan giraffe in the country in collaboration with the African Parks.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFchad-10) According to the tracking of giraffes' movements using GPS satellite tagging, some giraffe in the park spend significant time at boundaries of the park.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFchad-10)

The **Kordofan giraffe** (_**Giraffa antiquorum**_[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:1-2) or _**Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum**_) is a [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species "Species") or [subspecies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subspecies "Subspecies") of [giraffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giraffe "Giraffe") found in [northern Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Cameroon "Northern Cameroon"), southern [Chad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad "Chad"), the [Central African Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_African_Republic "Central African Republic"), and possibly [western Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Sudan "Western Sudan").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-range-3) They usually live in [tree savannas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna"), [bush savannas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steppe "Steppe") and [thorn savannas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4) Compared to most other subspecies, the Kordofan giraffe is relatively small at 3.8 to 4.7 m (12 ft 6 in to 15 ft 5 in),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-5) with more irregular spots on the inner legs. There are around 2,300 individuals living in the wild.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-6) In the wild, female Kordofan giraffes live in loose groups, whilst males live solitary.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4) They have an average lifespan of around 35 years.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)

_[The Christian Science Monitor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Christian\_Science\_Monitor "The Christian Science Monitor")_ lists only 38 individuals being alive in the embattled [Garamba National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park "Garamba National Park") in [The Democratic Republic of Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Democratic_Republic_of_Congo "The Democratic Republic of Congo") due to [poaching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poaching "Poaching"); their skin is used for [luxury goods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxury_goods "Luxury goods") and they are said to produce enough meat to feed poachers for weeks.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Recent genetic studies also shows distinct [genetic populations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_populations "Genetic populations") of giraffes that makes conservation of these subspecies even more important.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-7)

The population in the Bénoué Complex, Cameroon (a landscape that consists of three national parks: [Bénoué National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9nou%C3%A9_National_Park "Bénoué National Park"), [Faro National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faro_National_Park "Faro National Park"), [Bouba Njida National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bouba_Njida_National_Park "Bouba Njida National Park"); interconnected by 29 hunting zones), numbers fewer than 300 individuals as of 2023.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-onlinelibrary.wiley.com-8) Illegal hunting represents the greatest threat to the subspecies, particularly in [Bénoué National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9nou%C3%A9_National_Park "Bénoué National Park"), where it may become locally extinct without further conservation interventions.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-onlinelibrary.wiley.com-8)

The Kordofan giraffe eats a variety of sticks, leaves and bark, usually of [Acacia trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acacia "Acacia"). Additionally they eat grasses, buds, as well as seeds.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Like other giraffes, they classify as herbivores.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)

## Taxonomy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Taxonomy")]

Its English name is a reference to [Kordofan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan "Kordofan") in [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan "Sudan").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:1-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-range-3)

## Habitat

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Habitat")]

They are naturally found in northern [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon "Cameroon"), [Chad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad "Chad"), [Central African Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_African_Republic "Central African Republic") and [western Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan_(region) "Sudan (region)").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-range-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Kordofan giraffe live in [steppes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steppe "Steppe"), as well as [bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna"), [tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna") and [shrub savannas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4) Historically some confusion has existed over the exact range limit of this subspecies compared to the [West African giraffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_African_giraffe "West African giraffe"), with populations in e.g. northern [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon "Cameroon") formerly assigned to the latter.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Genetic work has also revealed that all "[West African giraffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_African_giraffe "West African giraffe")" in European [zoos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoo "Zoo") are in fact Kordofan giraffe.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) It has been suggested that the [Nigerian giraffe's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_African_giraffe "West African giraffe") ancestor dispersed from East to North Africa during the [Quaternary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaternary "Quaternary") period and thereafter migrated to its current [Sahel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahel "Sahel") distribution in West Africa in response to the development of the [Sahara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahara "Sahara") desert.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-range-3)

## Appearance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Appearance")]

The Kordofan giraffe has spots similarly to other giraffe subspecies. They are [even-toed ungulates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artiodactyl "Artiodactyl") and walk on long legs. Compared to other subspecies they are rather small; males are on average 6 m (19 ft 8 in) tall, females reach a height of 4.5 m (14 ft 9 in).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Their shoulder height lies between 2 metres (6 ft 7 in) for females to 3.5 metres (11 ft 6 in) for males.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) On top of that they have more irregular spots on the inner legs.

They have a blue tongue, which is around 50 centimetres (1 ft 8 in) long.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)

## Diet

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Diet")]

Like other giraffe subspecies, the Kordofan giraffe is a [herbivore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbivore "Herbivore"). Its diet consist of a variety of grasses, shrubs, buds, branches, leaves and bark, as well as seeds.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Their main food source comes from the [Acacia trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acacia "Acacia").

## Conservation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Conservation")]

Kordofan giraffe is one of most endangered giraffe subspecies. The population of kordofan giraffe declined more than 80% for last 35 years, IUCN Red List has classified the Kordofan giraffe as Critically Endangered species in 2018.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFchad-10)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-iucn-1)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Kordofan_giraffe_in_Garamba_National_Park.jpg/250px-Kordofan_giraffe_in_Garamba_National_Park.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kordofan_giraffe_in_Garamba_National_Park.jpg)

Kordofan giraffe in the [Garamba National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park "Garamba National Park"), DRC

In the [Garamba National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park "Garamba National Park") in DRC, their population was declined from 300 in 1976 to 100 in 2008.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-11) Another estimate is from 356 in 1993 to only 86 in 2007.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-thetimes-12) There also estimate that 86 in 2003 and only 38 in 2016.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-13) Most recent estimate is from 71 in 2022 to over 80 in 2024.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-14) Poaching is the greatest threat to Garamba's giraffe population.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-thetimes-12)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCF_DRC-15) It has brought Giraffe Conservation Foundation (GCF) collaboration with ICCN and African Parks and DRC's wildlife authority to save last giraffes in DRC since 2016.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCF_DRC-15) Fortunately, DRC government have successfully increased in Kordofan giraffe population in park to more than 90 individuals.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCF_DRC-15)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7d/Waza-NP-Giraffes.jpg/250px-Waza-NP-Giraffes.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Waza-NP-Giraffes.jpg)

A group of Kordofan giraffes in the [Waza National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waza_National_Park "Waza National Park"), Cameroon

In Bénoué Complex on Cameroon(a landscape that consists of three national parks: [Bénoué National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9nou%C3%A9_National_Park "Bénoué National Park"), [Faro National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faro_National_Park "Faro National Park"), [Bouba Njida National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bouba_Njida_National_Park "Bouba Njida National Park")); interconnected by 29 hunting zones), it is estimated fewer than 300 population remained in 2023. Illegal hunting is a major threat to giraffe in the Bénoué National Park, where it may become locally extinct without further conservation efforts.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-16) In an aerial survey by Wildlife Conservation Society of [Waza National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waza_National_Park "Waza National Park") it was revealed that at least 350 individuals remained.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFcameroon-17) GCF drafting the first-ever National Giraffe Conservation Strategy and Action Plan with together Cameroon government, to help conservation efforts for Kordofan giraffe in the country.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFcameroon-17)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ee/Girafe_du_parc_national_de_Zakouma.jpg/250px-Girafe_du_parc_national_de_Zakouma.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Girafe_du_parc_national_de_Zakouma.jpg)

Kordofan giraffe in the [Zakouma National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zakouma_National_Park "Zakouma National Park"), Chad

[Zakouma National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zakouma_National_Park "Zakouma National Park") of [Chad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad "Chad") is home to 60% of Kordofan giraffe remaining on earth.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFchad-10) According to a series of aerial surveys in park between 2005 and 2016, population of giraffe in park increased from 292 to 947.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-iucn-1) GCF drafting the first-ever conservation efforts for Kordofan giraffe in the country in collaboration with the African Parks.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFchad-10) According to the tracking of giraffes' movements using GPS satellite tagging, some giraffe in the park spend significant time at boundaries of the park.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFchad-10)

While there are just 47 Kordofan giraffe left in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), they are slowly on the rise. Only 3,000 remain in scattered populations across their range in Africa (with the largest population in Zakouma National Park in Chad), and these 47 in Garamba are the last of the subspecies living in the entire DRC. Insecurity, armed conflict and relentless poaching – where they were targeted simply for their tails which were sold as dowries - pushed them to the brink of extinction. By 2016, only 40 individuals remained. Protecting wildlife in Garamba has been particularly challenging given the size of the park, which spans 12,400 km2, and sits on the border with South Sudan. But we’ve seen a change in the last two years, and our law enforcement efforts are paying off. Elephant poaching is down 50% and this year, only two elephants have been lost. The last Kordofan Giraffe have had a few births, and are up to 47; and other key populations are either stable or on the increase. Our growing ranger force is also providing security to tens of thousands of people living around the park, creating safe places for new life, and hope, to return to this corner of the world again.

While there are just 47 Kordofan giraffe left in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), they are slowly on the rise. Only 3,000 remain in scattered populations across their range in Africa (with the largest population in Zakouma National Park in Chad), and these 47 in Garamba are the last of the subspecies living in the entire DRC. Insecurity, armed conflict and relentless poaching – where they were targeted simply for their tails which were sold as dowries - pushed them to the brink of extinction. By 2016, only 40 individuals remained. Protecting wildlife in Garamba has been particularly challenging given the size of the park, which spans 12,400 km2, and sits on the border with South Sudan. But we’ve seen a change in the last two years, and our law enforcement efforts are paying off. Elephant poaching is down 50% and this year, only two elephants have been lost. The last Kordofan Giraffe have had a few births, and are up to 47; and other key populations are either stable or on the increase. Our growing ranger force is also providing security to tens of thousands of people living around the park, creating safe places for new life, and hope, to return to this corner of the world again.

### Page note: https://www.africanparks.org/garambas-population-kordofan-giraffe-growing-heres-why
Reader state: complete; relevance: partial
Garamba National Park in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is the sole park in the country that hosts Kordofan giraffes (Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum).  As of the latest count in April 2025, the park’s Kordofan population has grown to **≈ 105 individuals**, up from 22 in 2012.  The subspecies, historically called the Congo giraffe, is now classified as Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum and is one of the seven extant giraffe subspecies.  Globally only about **7 000** northern giraffes remain, of which roughly **2 400** are Kordofan giraffes; the International Union for Conservation of Nature lists the subspecies as **Critically Endangered**.  Within Garamba the giraffes are found mainly in two breeding groups: the southern sector of the park and the adjacent Gangala na Bodio Hunting Domain.

**Page**

1 – “Garamba’s Population of Kordofan Giraffe is Growing – Here’s Why” (African Parks, 10 Sep 2025)

**Evidence**

- *Garamba National Park is home to the only population of giraffe in DRC* – “Garamba National Park is home to the only population of giraffe in DRC, and no ordinary giraffe at that.”
- *Population estimate (April 2025)* – “overall numbers of Kordofan giraffe in Garamba have risen to an estimated 105 at the last count (in April 2025; more on counting giraffe later in this blog).”
- *Earlier population figures* – “From an estimated population of 350 giraffe in the 1970s, only 22 remained in 2012 … overall numbers ... 70 in 2021, 92 in 2024.”
- *Subspecies identification* – “The Kordofan giraffe (named for the Kordofan region of central Sudan) is a subspecies of the northern giraffe… previously known as the Congo giraffe – Giraffa camelopardalis congolensis – but has since been reclassified as Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum.”
- *Global giraffe numbers* – “There are only around 7,000 northern giraffe left in the wild… Of these, approximately 2,400 belong to the Kordofan subspecies… listed by the IUCN as Critically Endangered.”
- *Distribution description* – “Kordofan giraffe ... occupies the savannah regions of the Sahel and Central Africa.”
- *Breeding group locations* – “Today, the population persists in two geographically distinct breeding groups: one in the southern sector of Garamba National Park and another in Gangala na Bodio Hunting Domain.”
- *Conservation partnership* – “The partnership between Garamba National Park and the Giraffe Conservation Foundation was formalised in 2012 and renewed in 2025...”.
